local_convergence_argument.accuracy_and_cost: For any epsilon>0 and supplied C>=C_exact, C>0, T=max(1,ceil(s^(-1) max(0,log(C/epsilon)))) ensures e_T<=epsilon because rho^T<=exp(-sT). If C=0, e_T=0 for every T and choose T=1. A common computable bound C may require separate aggregation; this proof does not give an uncharged distributed stopping test. For this choice T<=1+2sqrt(kappa_l) max(0,log(C/epsilon)) and amended time T(1+K tau)+1 <=(1+tau/sqrt(gamma))[1+2sqrt(kappa_l) max(0,log(C/epsilon))]+1 (use zero log term when C=0). Exactly K W multiplications occur per gossip: one at initialization and K-1 in the subloop. The final evaluation adds one exact local call per node, no gossip, and does not alter the prefix. With fixed instance parameters this gives the source's logarithmic-accuracy form and all-node convergence. It asserts no uniform initialization-free bound: C can depend on kappa_l and instance data; log(C/epsilon) and any resulting log(kappa_l) are retained.
local_convergence_argument.conjugacy: For every x, f_i(theta)-<x,theta> has a coercive quadratic lower bound from strong convexity, so continuity and strong convexity give a unique minimizer p with grad f_i(p)=x. The strong-convexity lower quadratic bound at p, maximized in the Fenchel supremum, gives f_i*(z)<=f_i*(x)+<p,z-x>+||z-x||^2/(2alpha). The beta-smooth upper quadratic bound at p, evaluated in that supremum at p+(z-x)/beta, gives f_i*(z)>=f_i*(x)+<p,z-x>+||z-x||^2/(2beta). The two inequalities imply differentiability with grad f_i*(x)=p and establish 1/alpha smoothness and 1/beta strong convexity. Summing gives these properties for F*(X)=sum_i f_i*(x_i), without a Hessian assumption.
local_convergence_argument.dual_transform: Let H={Z:Z1=0}, A=P^(1/2), and A^dagger its inverse on H (zero on constants). For D in H, a0||D||^2<=||DA||^2<=b0||D||^2. Thus g(Z)=F*(ZA) on H is L=b0/alpha smooth and m=a0/beta strongly convex, with grad g(Z)=grad F*(ZA) A in H. Let theta* be the unique minimizer of fbar, which exists by global strong convexity/coercivity, and X* have columns grad f_i(theta*). Then X*1=0, Z*=X*A^dagger is in H, Z*A=X*, and grad g(Z*)=theta*1^T A=0. It is the unique minimizer. X_t,Y_t remain in H by induction from zero and P1=0. Put Z_t=X_t A^dagger, B_t=Y_t A^dagger, s=sqrt(m/L)=(1-q)/((1+q)sqrt(kappa_l)), rho=1-s. Here 0<s<1. Because PA^dagger=A, the exact recurrence becomes B_{t+1}=Z_t-grad g(Z_t)/L and Z_{t+1}=(1+mu)B_{t+1}-mu B_t, with B_0=Z_0=0. Direct substitution gives eta=1/L and mu=(1-s)/(1+s). A and A^dagger are analysis devices only.
local_convergence_argument.output_and_initialization: Strong monotonicity of grad f_i applied to theta_{i,t}=grad f_i*(x_{i,t}) and theta* gives alpha||theta_{i,t}-theta*||^2<=<x_{i,t}-x_i*,theta_{i,t}-theta*>; Cauchy-Schwarz yields ||theta_{i,t}-theta*||<=||x_{i,t}-x_i*||/alpha. Since fbar is beta-smooth and stationary at theta*, 0<=e_t=max_i[fbar(theta_{i,t})-fbar(theta*)]<=beta||X_t-X*||^2/(2alpha^2)<=C_exact rho^t, with C_exact=beta b0 E_0/(alpha^2 m). The same state bound proves all-node convergence. Let Theta_0 collect grad f_i*(0), and G0^2=||grad g(0)||^2=trace(Theta_0 P Theta_0^T). Minimizing the m-strong-convexity quadratic lower bound at 0 gives g(0)-g(Z*)<=G0^2/(2m); strong monotonicity and grad g(Z*)=0 give ||Z*||<=G0/m. Therefore E_0<=G0^2/m and C_exact<=C_init=beta b0 G0^2/(alpha^2 m^2). Also G0^2<=b0||Theta_0||^2. These are instance-dependent constants derived under the original assumptions, not assumed bounds on the functions.
local_convergence_argument.polynomial: Let C_0(z)=1,C_1(z)=z,C_{j+1}(z)=2zC_j(z)-C_{j-1}(z). Induction on the actual scalar and matrix gossip recurrences gives a_j=C_j(c2), Z_j=U C_j(c2(I-c3W)); hence gossip returns UP, P=I-C_K(c2(I-c3W))/C_K(c2). For each positive eigenvalue lambda in [gamma lambda_1,lambda_1], c2(1-c3 lambda) is in [-1,1], by substituting both endpoints. The recurrence gives C_j(cos theta)=cos(j theta), hence |C_K(z)|<=1 on this interval. Set a=(1+u)/(1-u)=c1^(-1). Since c2=(a+a^(-1))/2, the same recurrence gives C_K(c2)=(a^K+a^(-K))/2=(1+q^2)/(2q). Thus P has kernel span(1) and positive eigenvalues in [a0,b0], where r=2q/(1+q^2), a0=1-r>0 and b0=1+r. At lambda=0 the polynomial is zero. For K=floor(1/u), u>1/(K+1), so c1<K/(K+2) and q<(1+2/K)^(-K)<=1/3, the last inequality following from Bernoulli (1+2/K)^K>=3. Therefore sqrt(b0/a0)=(1+q)/(1-q)<2 and K<=1/sqrt(gamma). This proves the required spectral bound without external minimax or Chebyshev theorems.
local_convergence_argument.potential: Define V_0=0, Z_t=(B_t+sV_t)/(1+s), V_{t+1}=(1-s)V_t+sZ_t-(s/m)grad g(Z_t). Substitution using s^2=m/L shows these identities reproduce the preceding momentum recurrence for all t (equivalently (B_{t+1}+sV_{t+1})/(1+s)=(1+mu)B_{t+1}-mu B_t). Let E_t=g(B_t)-g(Z*)+(m/2)||V_t-Z*||^2. To prove E_{t+1}<=rho E_t, write h=grad g(Z_t) and U=(1-s)(V_t-Z*)+s(Z_t-Z*). Smoothness gives g(B_{t+1})<=g(Z_t)-||h||^2/(2L). Expanding the potential norm gives (m/2)||U||^2-s<U,h>+s^2||h||^2/(2m); the gradient-square terms cancel. Using the weighted squared-norm identity yields E_{t+1}<=g(Z_t)-g(Z*)+(1-s)(m/2)||V_t-Z*||^2+s(m/2)||Z_t-Z*||^2-s(1-s)(m/2)||V_t-Z_t||^2-s<Z_t-Z*,h>-s(1-s)<V_t-Z_t,h>. Strong convexity at Z_t gives g(Z*)>=g(Z_t)+<h,Z*-Z_t>+(m/2)||Z_t-Z*||^2. Apply it to s times the function gap to obtain E_{t+1}<=(1-s)[(m/2)||V_t-Z*||^2+g(Z_t)-g(Z*)-s<V_t-Z_t,h>-s(m/2)||V_t-Z_t||^2]. Since B_t-Z_t=s(Z_t-V_t), convexity gives g(B_t)>=g(Z_t)-s<V_t-Z_t,h>. Dropping the nonpositive squared term proves contraction. Thus E_t<=rho^t E_0, E_0=g(0)-g(Z*)+(m/2)||Z*||^2. Nonnegativity of the function gap and strong convexity imply both ||B_t-Z*||^2 and ||V_t-Z*||^2 are <=2E_t/m. Their convex combination Z_t obeys the same bound, so ||X_t-X*||^2<=2b0 E_0 rho^t/m. This controls the actual extrapolated query state, not only Y_t.

local_convergence_argument.source_display_issue: Supplement p.2 Eq.(12)'s intermediate comparison is not adopted. For W=[[5/12,-1/12,-1/3],[-1/12,5/12,-1/3],[-1/3,-1/3,2/3]], the orthogonal eigenvectors (1,1,1),(1,-1,0),(1,1,-2) have eigenvalues 0,1/2,1. This is valid complete-graph gossip, gamma=1/2, K=1, c1=3-2sqrt(2), and P=(4/3)W. Thus 1/sqrt(gamma(P))=sqrt(2). The displayed intermediate ratio uses c1^(sqrt(2)+1). Since sqrt(2)+1>2 and 0<c1<1, that ratio is less than (1+c1^2)/(1-c1^2)=3/(2sqrt(2))<sqrt(2), contradicting the displayed comparison. The separate floor-K argument above recovers the useful bound <2; neither the Source record nor its printed formula is changed.
local_convergence_argument.statement: Define fbar(theta)=(1/n)sum_i f_i(theta), and theta*=argmin fbar. For every finite n>=2, d>=1, every differentiable alpha-strongly convex beta-smooth f_i:R^d->R with 0<alpha<=beta, every fixed graph-supported symmetric PSD W with ker(W)=span(1) and 0<gamma<1, the selected recurrence from X_0=Y_0=0 with its printed tuning has the bounds below for every integer t>=0. With exact local conjugate Oracle and the extra terminal evaluation, every integer T>=1 returns theta_{i,T} satisfying max_i[fbar(theta_{i,T})-fbar(theta*)]<=C_exact rho^T and theta_{i,T}->theta*. There is no randomness, Hessian assumption, bound on translations of f_i or extra assumed convergence premise. tau>=0 is the communication-round charge. All matrix norms and inner products below are Frobenius unless specified.

terminal_repair_proposal.amendment: After the unchanged T-iteration loop, evaluate theta_{i,T}=grad f_i*(x_{i,T}) once at each node and return these vectors. This preserves the declared terminal index and all original assumptions. It does not substitute theta_{i,T-1}.
terminal_repair_proposal.full_local_argument: For every x in R^d, h(theta)=f_i(theta)-<x,theta> is alpha-strongly convex. Its strong-convexity lower bound at 0 is a quadratic with positive leading coefficient, so h is coercive. Continuity yields a minimizer p, strong convexity makes it unique, and differentiability gives grad f_i(p)=x. Thus the selected exact conjugate Oracle returns a finite, unique p=grad f_i*(x); the proposed terminal call is well-defined. It does not alter any x_t or y_t. A run with budget T+1 has exactly the same states through x_T,y_T because budget T only controls loop termination and all tuning parameters are independent of T. Its first operation at t=T is precisely this terminal call. Hence the proposed returned vector equals the t=T primal-recovery vector of the unchanged infinite recurrence. For a quantitative transfer, let theta* minimize fbar and define x_i*=grad f_i(theta*); then sum_i x_i*=0 by first-order optimality. Strong convexity, applied in both directions and added, gives <grad f_i(p)-grad f_i(theta*),p-theta*> >= alpha||p-theta*||^2. Substituting grad f_i(p)=x_{i,T} and applying Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||theta_{i,T}-theta*|| <= ||x_{i,T}-x_i*||/alpha, including the zero-distance case. Since fbar is beta-smooth and grad fbar(theta*)=0, its smoothness upper bound gives 0<=fbar(theta_{i,T})-fbar(theta*) <= beta||x_{i,T}-x_i*||^2/(2 alpha^2). Therefore max_i primal objective error is at most beta||x_T-x*||_F^2/(2 alpha^2). This transfer inequality is completed by the unconditional bound for the actual MSDA query state in #/content/local_convergence_argument; no convergence premise is added to the assumptions.

variants.output: After the unchanged loop, evaluate theta_{i,T}=grad f_i*(x_{i,T}) once at every node and return it. public_inputs: Integer iteration budget T>=1; graph-supported gossip W; known alpha,beta with 0<alpha<=beta; lambda_1(W) and gamma=lambda_{n-1}(W)/lambda_1(W).
variants.query_and_update: For t=0,...,T-1, compute theta_{i,t}=grad f_i*(x_{i,t}) at every node and assemble Theta_t. Set y_{t+1}=x_t-eta AcceleratedGossip(Theta_t,W,K), then x_{t+1}=(1+mu)y_{t+1}-mu y_t. For input U, AcceleratedGossip initializes a_0=1,a_1=c2,Z_0=U,Z_1=c2 U(I-c3 W). For k=1,...,K-1 set a_{k+1}=2 c2 a_k-a_{k-1}, Z_{k+1}=2 c2 Z_k(I-c3 W)-Z_{k-1}; return Z_0-Z_K/a_K. Z disambiguates the subroutine state from outer x_t. After the loop make the separately charged terminal conjugate-gradient call specified in output.
variants.requirements: Connected undirected graph with n>=2. Each f_i:R^d→R is alpha-strongly convex and beta-smooth in the Euclidean norm. W is symmetric PSD, ker(W)=span(1), and off-diagonal nonzero entries require graph edges. Each node has exact grad f_i*; multiplication of a distributed d×n matrix by W uses one neighbor communication round. Graph and parameters are fixed.
variants.state_and_initialization: Matrices x_0=y_0=0 in R^{d×n}; local columns x_{i,t},y_{i,t}. Theta_t collects local primal columns. Restricted to 0<gamma<1; kappa_l=beta/alpha>=1.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Let u=sqrt(gamma), c1=(1-u)/(1+u), c2=(1+gamma)/(1-gamma), c3=2/((1+gamma)lambda_1(W)), K=floor(1/u), q=c1^K, kappa_l=beta/alpha. Use eta=alpha(1+q^2)/(1+q)^2 and mu=((1+q)sqrt(kappa_l)-1+q)/((1+q)sqrt(kappa_l)+1-q). Stop after supplied integer T>=1, then make the terminal call. For epsilon>0 and supplied C>=C_exact defined in the local argument, choose T=max(1,ceil(s^(-1) max(0,log(C/epsilon)))) with s=(1-q)/((1+q)sqrt(kappa_l)); C=0 permits any T>=1. This is a supplied-budget rule, not a distributed adaptive stopping protocol. Acquiring a common valid C can require separately charged aggregation/preprocessing.
